items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity is high for fleet-wide go-live, new public exposure, and security-sensitive releases. Evidence: the 2026-10-01 security baseline covers 61 managed sites, but fleet-doctor has no run, checks, findings, or site results; operations has no deploy, uptime, or error-sweep results; and authentication/access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS configuration, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are not evidenced. Compliance is technical-only with 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown, not certification. Decision: preserve existing public-exposure and security-sensitive release gates; permit only ordinary reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Do not claim a clean bill of health.

Security recommendation: retain the existing private gate for the gated product. Source-rights, data-flow, consent and analytics, vendor/logging, incident, security, accuracy, measurement, and owner gates remain incomplete. No public exposure, notification expansion, remarketing, monetization change, credential change, deployment, dependency addition, or external outreach is authorized.

items.title: Maintain evidence-needed fleet security disposition and release gates
items.summary: Fleet security clearance is unsupported because fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results and material security controls remain unevidenced. Preserve public-exposure and security-sensitive release gates while continuing bounded read-only evidence work.
items.requested_action: Complete the canonical read-only control matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Permit ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, deploy, add dependencies, request duplicate telemetry, or claim certification.
